core_obligations: Record that base change is exact, so the cohomology of the base change is the base change of the cohomology (proof lines 16457-16461).
Let n be the largest degree with nonvanishing cohomology and observe that it is also the largest such degree after base change (proof lines 16462-16465).
Settle the case where n is below m using the characterisation of m-pseudo-coherence (proof lines 16463-16464).
Descend finiteness of the top cohomology module and lift a surjection from a finite free module to a map of complexes (proof lines 16466-16474).
Apply the induction hypothesis to the cone, whose base change is m-pseudo-coherent by the cone lemma, and conclude by the cone lemma again (proof lines 16475-16484).
proof_roadmap: Set up the induction and the top degree (proof lines 16457-16465).
Descend finiteness and build the approximation (proof lines 16466-16474).
Apply induction to the cone and conclude (proof lines 16475-16484).
difficulty_reason: The lemma descends m-pseudo-coherence of a complex along a faithfully flat ring map. The proof follows the same induction as the local version for a finite cover: exactness of base change identifies the cohomology of the base changed complex, the top degree in which cohomology can be nonzero is unchanged, and the bounding case is read off from the characterisation of m-pseudo-coherence. In the remaining case finiteness of the top cohomology after base change descends back to the ring by faithfully flat descent of module properties, a surjection from a finite free module is lifted to a map of complexes, and the cone, whose cohomology vanishes in the top degrees and whose base change is still m-pseudo-coherent by the cone lemma, is handled by the induction hypothesis before the cone lemma is applied once more.
